scope: Existing review questions only; no new sources or human approvals

records.answer: Source error remains unresolved: page 3 literally calls secure tenure a barrier, while reference 35 on page 5 concerns carbon outcomes of land-cover transitions in Southeast Asia. Removed the previously inferred positive direction. Neither reversing the sentence nor treating the reference as tenure evidence is justified. Retain the source wording for audit; no tenure-direction vote or executable rule.

Restored citation chain: FAO reports Sanogo et al. (2000), cited through Yossi et al. (2006). Non-adopters report shortages of labour, land, planting material or time. This is secondary evidence of reported adoption barriers, not an isolated causal labour effect. The intermediary and original do not become extra independent votes.

Corrected to planting-material availability. Page 48 concerns seed/cutting supply for live fences, not product markets. FAO attributes the supply constraint to Satin (1998) and FIDA (1995), including PAGF restrictions and pressure on natural Euphorbia stands. Retain as secondary operational evidence; new variable has no spatial binding or numeric curve.

Page 11 is the review authors’ synthesis of contexts where FMNR has been studied: 100–950 mm/year and low-fertility soils. It explicitly says suitability outside these contexts needs research. The following Bayala citation supports the separate soil-carbon statement. Retained as observed context, not preferred rainfall/soil limits; no direction or threshold vote. This source is Chomba et al. (2020); Lohbeck is a coauthor and the stable source ID is retained.

Page 11 is the review authors’ synthesis of contexts where FMNR has been studied: 100–950 mm/year and low-fertility soils. It explicitly says suitability outside these contexts needs research. The following Bayala citation supports the separate soil-carbon statement. Retained as observed context, not preferred rainfall/soil limits; no direction or threshold vote. This source is Chomba et al. (2020); Lohbeck is a coauthor and the stable source ID is retained.

Restored the complete sentence and citations. The review attributes tenure constraints to Chomba et al. (2016) and Binam et al. (2017). Retain secondary operational guidance, not a new independent field study or numeric tenure rule; originals still require claim-specific verification.

Restored the complete governance claim and Binam et al. (2017) citation. The passage bundles farmer choices, tenure, policy, grazing by-laws and conflict management. Keep attributed qualitative operational guidance; it does not isolate a governance coefficient or justify multiple independent source votes.

Confirmed rainfall is used in the Sengon assessment: Table 3 identifies water availability as a limiting factor, and page 6 links it to annual rainfall. Count model use in the species-specific lane. No rainfall cutoff or monotonic direction is supplied; land-unit identifiers are local study labels, not ontology variables.

Class VII is a general land-capability category, not an agroforestry suitability score. The text associates it with slopes above 45% and severe cultivation limitations, allowing grazing/forest uses. The paper’s agroforestry conclusion instead names classes III and IV. Retained the class definition as context; no universal 45% agroforestry cutoff inferred.

Confirmed Table 5 is a summary of land-mapping units used to describe the study landscape. Its 8–72% slope span is not an agroforestry establishment envelope. Removed the encoded absolute minimum/maximum and retained the five observed bands. Existing dropped status stays unchanged.

This passage is the author’s qualitative interpretation of information barriers and producer beliefs, not a measured cause-and-effect result. It reports a belief about shade and grazing which the author calls scientifically unfounded. Retain as expert operational context; no causal coefficient or numeric suitability rule.

Corrected variable to gender differences in participation/adoption. Page 7 reports female-headed households less likely to participate or practise FMNR, with eight/five percent in parentheses. Their denominator and percent-versus-percentage-point meaning are not defined in this passage, so retained verbatim without computing an effect. Footnote 6 limits the land-ownership sensitivity check to FMNR East Africa. This informs inclusion/implementation, not a national gender index or core T4 score.

The source concerns access to markets for selling tree products. Retained in the broad market/value-chain group with a clear source label. The authors contrast two sublocations and recommend infrastructure/cooperatives; this passage gives no measured distance or travel-time response. It cannot calibrate those spatial proxies.
